title: Size the rate limiter's counter store
scenario: A distributed rate limiter checks two rules on every request against a shared in-memory counter store. Use decimal units (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes). Anything within 25% counts.

questions.prompt: Counter operations per second at peak
Memory for all counters, one copy
Store operations per second if the busiest keys (60% of traffic) take tokens in batches of 10

solution:
1. **Operations:** 500,000 requests × 2 rules = **1,000,000 counter operations per second** if each rule is a separate operation. (Checking both rules in one atomic call halves the round trips but not the work.)
2. **Shards:** 1,000,000 ÷ 100,000 = 10 shards at full load, × 2 for headroom = **20 shards**.
3. **Memory:** 10,000,000 keys × 2 rules × 100 bytes = 2 × 10⁹ bytes = **2 GB**. Memory is not the constraint; throughput is.
4. **Leases:** 60% of operations (600,000) shrink 10× to 60,000; the other 40% (400,000) stay. Total ≈ **460,000 operations per second**, which saves several shards at the cost of a small overshoot for the heaviest keys.
